facts.statement: The genus Limenavis was named by Clarke and Chiappe in 2001.
Limenavis lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Campanian-Maastrichtian boundary of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It lived about 70 million years ago, around the Campanian-Maastrichtian boundary.

facts.statement: The only known species, Limenavis patagonica, was discovered in the lower member of the Allen Formation at Salitral Moreno, 20 km south of General Roca in Río Negro, Argentina.
facts.quote: Known from several broken bones, the remains of the only known species Limenavis patagonica were found in rocks of the "lower member" of the Allen Formation at Salitral Moreno, 20 km south of General Roca, Río Negro (Argentina).

facts.statement: Limenavis is a genus of ornithuran dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Limenavis is a genus of ornithuran dinosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Limenavis patagonica is considered one of the stem-bird species closest to the common ancestor of all modern birds.
facts.quote: Of all the stem-birds known to date, this species is among those closest to the common ancestor of all living birds.

facts.statement: The name Limenavis translates to "bird of the threshold" or "limit-bird", combining the Latin words for threshold and bird.
facts.quote: Limenavis, meaning "bird of the threshold" or "limit-bird", is derived from Latin limen ("threshold") + avis ("bird").

facts.statement: The species name patagonica indicates that the fossil was found in Patagonia.
facts.quote: The specific name patagonica refers to the specimen's Patagonian provenance.

facts.statement: Early analyses by Clarke and Chiappe classified Limenavis as a member of Carinatae that was more advanced than Ichthyornis but not part of the modern bird group Neornithes.
facts.quote: Analyses published in 2001 and 2002 by Julia Clarke and Luis Chiappe found Limenavis to be a member of Carinatae more advanced than Ichthyornis but not a member of the modern bird group Neornithes.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by O'Connor and colleagues suggested that Limenavis is slightly more primitive than Ichthyornis.
facts.quote: A 2013 analysis by O'Connor and colleagues found it to be slightly more primitive than Ichthyornis.

facts.statement: The parent group of Limenavis is Ornithurae.
The time range for Limenavis is the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers have suggested that certain features of Limenavis might link it to paleognath birds, possibly related to the ancestors of tinamous or rheas.
rejected.quote: It has been suggested that some features link it with paleognath birds, perhaps related to the ancestors of tinamous or rheas.
